_comment: Campaign 31 on the Mac (2026-11-13, Jack: 'try training on the mac ... see how long a generation takes'). configs/run_c31.json continued from c31's best (gen 27) with an empty replay buffer while the box was down. Launch: PYTHONPATH=build:. python -m src.v2.train.train --config configs/run_c31_mac.json --init-weights checkpoints/remote/campaign31/gen_0027.pt. A worker would otherwise run all of its assigned games at once (selfplay.n_games is ignored when a slot manifest is used) and the 1024 games of a generation would hold about 88 GB of search trees whatever parallel_workers is, so selfplay.max_concurrent_games 64 plays each worker's 128 games in waves (at most 512 games, about 44 GB, at once) to fit a 64 GB Mac. Two attempts without the cap on the M1 Max were stopped in self-play (45k server evals/s, GPU-bound, no game finished); see docs/benchmarks.md. 2026-11-14 (Jack): cap removed (0) after the 2-player/32-pile engine cut tree memory ~37%; measured 512 concurrent games ~22 GB of workers, so all 1024 at once should be ~50 GB. Differences from run_c31.json, all hardware: self-play served by MLX fp16 on Metal (server_device mps, server_backend mlx, server_fp16) instead of the compiled bf16 CUDA graph (server_compile, server_autocast_bf16, server_trim_piles, server_batch_buckets off; eager paths trim tokens per batch); 8 workers instead of 64; one server shard; 8 eval workers. Two schedule differences because generation numbering restarts at 1: the human anchor is held at 0.1 (where c31 had it from gen 20), and the cosine learning rate restarts from 1.4e-4. League seeds point at the local copies of c29 gen 10/25/35. Gate (2026-11-15): gate_backend mlx fp32 (identical games to PyTorch over 50,861 decisions, ~1.4x faster; fp16 bought no gate speed) and gate_chunk 400 (the gate was 90% evaluation at 333-row batches).
